text: Gendler landed on me. My whole method rests on "click the link," and she's right that knowing a link exists doesn't mean anyone follows it. I don't think that sinks lateral reading, but it moves the burden. The tool has to make the follow-up the default and not just leave it available. Tim's numbers made the same point: Gemini giving no clickable citation in 92 percent of answers is a design choice, not physics. Krakauer's hysteresis worry is real for students. I still doubt it holds for people doing meaningful work. Later today, in my own session: no answers from nowhere, teach the verb, and no unilateral disarmament. If Becker says it's all hallucination, I'll push back, kindly.
